options.text: Deploy shared AVD services: Secrets and Encryption Key Vaults, Log Analytics and AVD Insights resources, and an FSLogix Recovery Services vault with an Azure Files snapshot backup policy. Run this deployment before host pools, image management, or add-ons that consume these shared resources.

elements.name: subscription
elements.label: Operations Resources Subscription
elements.toolTip: Select the workload subscription for the operations resource group, Key Vaults, and FSLogix Recovery Services vault.

elements.name: location
elements.label: Region
elements.toolTip: Select the Azure region for all Shared Services resources. Operations and monitoring resources can use different subscriptions but share this region.

options.text: Configure shared Key Vault, FSLogix backup, and private endpoint resources in the workload subscription selected on Deployment Basics.

elements.name: deployFSLogixBackupVault
elements.label: Deploy FSLogix Backup Vault and Policy

options.text: Optionally deploy one regional Recovery Services vault and Azure Files snapshot backup policy for FSLogix profile storage. The vault is shared by pooled host pools and standalone FSLogix storage deployments. Profile snapshots remain in each storage account; the vault stores backup policy and scheduling metadata.

constraints.validationMessage: Use 1-150 letters, numbers, underscores, or hyphens.

elements.name: retentionDays
elements.label: Daily Snapshot Retention (Days)
elements.toolTip: Number of daily Azure Files snapshots retained by the shared snapshot-tier policy (1-200).

elements.name: timeZone
elements.label: Backup Policy Time Zone
elements.toolTip: Select the Windows time zone used by the daily backup schedule.

allowedValues.label: (UTC+01:00) Amsterdam, Berlin, Bern, Rome, Stockholm, Vienna

options.text: The Secrets Key Vault (Standard SKU) stores AVD credentials: VM local administrator and domain join account. Downstream deployers reference this vault by resource ID only — they do not need read access to the secrets themselves. To read secrets at deployment time (e.g., for getSecret() ARM references), the deploying identity needs the 'Key Vault Secrets User' role.

elements.name: enableSoftDelete
elements.label: Enable Soft Delete
elements.toolTip: Allow recovery of deleted Key Vault objects within the retention period.

elements.name: enablePurgeProtection
elements.label: Enable Purge Protection
elements.toolTip: Prevent permanent deletion of the Key Vault and its objects during the retention period. Strongly recommended for production environments.

elements.name: retentionDays
elements.label: Soft Delete Retention (Days)
elements.toolTip: Number of days to retain soft-deleted Key Vault objects before permanent deletion.

options.text: Provide the AVD session host credentials to store in the Secrets Key Vault. All fields are optional — you can store credentials later by re-running this deployment. Domain join credentials are only required for ADDS or Entra Kerberos hybrid environments.

elements.name: virtualMachineAdminUserName
elements.label: Admin Username
elements.toolTip: Local administrator username for AVD session hosts. Stored as 'VirtualMachineAdminUserName' in the Key Vault.

constraints.validationMessage: Must start with a letter. Alphanumeric, underscores, hyphens allowed. Maximum 20 characters.

elements.name: virtualMachineAdminPassword
elements.toolTip: Local administrator password for AVD session hosts. Stored as 'VirtualMachineAdminPassword' in the Key Vault. Must meet Windows password complexity requirements.

constraints.validationMessage: Must be 12-123 characters and include uppercase, lowercase, a digit, and a special character.

elements.name: domainJoinUserPrincipalName
elements.label: Domain Join UPN
elements.toolTip: UPN of the privileged account used to domain join session hosts. Stored as 'DomainJoinUserPrincipalName' in the Key Vault.

constraints.validationMessage: Must be a valid UPN format (user@domain.tld).

elements.name: domainJoinUserPassword
elements.toolTip: Password for the domain join account. Stored as 'DomainJoinUserPassword' in the Key Vault.

options.text: The Encryption Key Vault (Premium SKU) can hold RSA-4096 or RSA-HSM keys for AVD customer-managed encryption. Select CMK and HSM protection according to applicable key-control, authorization, and policy requirements. Consuming deployments can use this vault or an existing compatible vault; creating a new Shared Services vault is not universally required. Key creation requires permissions such as the 'Key Vault Crypto Officer' role.

elements.name: encKvRetentionInDays
elements.label: Encryption Key Vault Soft Delete Retention (Days)
elements.toolTip: Number of days the Encryption Key Vault and its objects are retained after deletion before permanent removal.

options.text: Define your naming convention using the components below. The defaults follow the Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF) naming convention: {resource-type}-avd-{identifier}-{region}. Adjust the component order, separator, workload value, or abbreviations to match your organization's standard.

options.text: Select the components that make up your naming convention and arrange them in order using Component 1 through Component 6. Select 'None (stop here)' to end the sequence. Auto-resolved components — Resource Type, Purpose, Location — are substituted per resource at deployment time. Value components — Workload, Environment, Free-form Text 1, Free-form Text 2 — require you to supply a value in the fields that appear below.

Recommended components for conflict-free, identifiable names: Required - Resource Type (identifies the resource category: rg, kv, pe, nic), Purpose (distinguishes the secrets and encryption Key Vaults), Workload (scopes names to your application or project). Highly Recommended - Location (prevents name collisions when deploying across regions).

No 'Purpose' component selected. Both Key Vaults in this deployment (secrets and encryption) will have identical names. Including 'Purpose' is required.

No 'Workload' component selected. Including Workload is strongly recommended - it scopes resource names to your application or project and prevents collisions with other deployments using the same convention.
No 'Location' component selected. If you plan to deploy Key Vaults in multiple regions, include Location in your convention to avoid resource name conflicts between deployments.
Duplicate component detected. Each component type can only appear once in the naming convention. Please ensure each selected component is unique.

Generated Key Vault names must not exceed 24 characters. Shorten the naming convention or enter complete Secrets and Encryption Key Vault name overrides for the vaults being deployed. Overlength generated names fail deployment; they are not truncated.
No location segment in your naming convention — a location code is automatically included in the Key Vault unique string seed to prevent name collisions across regions.
